previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and obesity, was admitted for an acute worsening of chronic neck and back pain, rated as severe and limiting mobility and sleep. He presented after failing to reach his pain physician for medication refills. Initial management included IV hydromorphone and ketorolac for breakthrough pain, with continuation of home medications including OxyContin, duloxetine, and inhalers. Imaging showed no fracture but was limited by body habitus; chest X-ray revealed atelectasis without pneumonia. Inflammatory markers improved during the stay. Rheumatology and pain consultants supported symptom management without restarting biologics due to patient's prior infection concerns. Pain control improved, allowing ambulation and discharge home on unchanged narcotics. Follow-up includes continued primary care management of pain, outpatient physical therapy, and ongoing monitoring of ankylosing spondylitis.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old male with past medical history of 
hypertension, obesity, ankylosing spondylitis not currently on 
DMARD therapy, with prior presentations for pain control, 
admitted ___ with L sacroiliac joint pain typical of 
prior flares, seen by rheumatology and started on steroids, 
discharged home. 

# Ankylosing spondylitis of lumbarsacral area, with acute flare
# L sacroiliac joint pain 
# Opiate dependence 
Patient has declined any DMARDs for his ankylosing spondylitis 
due to prior infections and/or intolerances, and has had 
several recent admissions for pain control issues.  He is 
managed on a narcotics contract with his outpatient provider.  
Patient declined any imaging due to his concerns regarding 
radiation exposure.  CRP stable from prior values.  He was seen 
by rheumatology, who felt that there could be contribution of 
mild SI flare-up, and recommended that, ""Even though, steroids 
are not indicated for AS treatment, this is atypical patient 
and in the past he was responding to lower doses of steroids"".  
Patient was started on a short steroid taper (Prednisone 30mg 
x3 days, followed by 20mgPO x3 days, followed by 10 mg PO x 3 
days, then stop).  Symptoms improved and he was able to be 
discharged home. Per discussion with outpatient provider, he 
was given a 3 day prescription of his outpatient opiates to 
last until he would be able to pick up his chronic narcotics 
contract prescription .
